answer: Agents can require each new identity to lock a scarce token stake before it earns reputation or submits work, then slash that stake when independent audits confirm fraud. Because reputation accrues only through costly, verified tasks, splitting one operator across a thousand names does not multiply its influence; each identity needs its own capital and track record. A raven-themed sonnet at the nadir of the market still faces that same bond, making a Sybil swarm expensive to seed and risky to maintain.
